correctness.rationale: With unit mass, complex polarization reduces energy exactness to vanishing of the nonzero Fourier moments in the full integer difference box [-2N,2N]^2. Integration over a complete primitive loop kills every character except multiples of its primitive perpendicular vector, so each off-diagonal Gram entry can come from only one unoriented direction. For a direction of mass W>0 and m=max(|p|,|q|), this gives the vanishing moments of orders 1 through T=floor(2N/m). The normalized moment Gram matrix of powers 0 through T is the identity; its rank gives L>=T+1 even with repeated offsets. In equality its square weighted Vandermonde matrix is unitary, giving equal internal weights and a translated root polygon by column orthogonality (for T=0 there is simply one arbitrary offset). The physical length is at least 2π(T+1)m>=2π(2N+1), and equality forces Euclidean length of the primitive vector to equal m, hence a coordinate direction, then exactly 2N+1 circles. Summing gives the asserted equality configurations for J=1 and J=2, with arbitrary positive total weights per coordinate family in the latter, and strictness for J>=3. The numerical checker was inspected but not run; its bounded corroboration is not used to prove the result.
residual_risks: No extension to partial curves, signed weight schemes or travel between distinct components is verified or required.

value.rationale: A sharp cost within the class of complete straight periodic acquisition loops matters because combining slopes and choosing independent weights could otherwise enlarge the design space. The separate moment criterion rules out that tradeoff, gives an exact component count for each prescribed slope, and characterizes both attainment and strictness of the global length bound. This goes beyond the known parallel equal-weight optimum without asserting a bound for general connected sampling paths.
residual_risks: Value is in exact cubature and trajectory length, not stability or connected-path cost.
